title: Thousands rally in Madrid to demand guarantees for state pension scheme
seoTitle: Madrid rally supporting state pension scheme

tea.why: Protesters marched to demand protections for Spain's state pension scheme amid political rows ahead of a parliamentary election.
tea.want: Demonstrators demanded pension guarantees, pensions to remain indexed to inflation, and the elimination of the gender pension gap.
tea.changed: Oct 24: 25,000 to 50,000 people rallied in central Madrid from Atocha train station to Gran Via.

summary: Tens of thousands of people marched through central Madrid on Saturday to demand robust protections and guarantees for Spain's state pension scheme. Organised in the lead-up to an upcoming parliamentary election, demonstrators walked from Atocha train station to the Gran Via, carrying banners with slogans such as "protect and guarantee our pensions" and chanting for pensions to remain indexed to inflation. Participants expressed concern that the pension system could be weakened or privatised depending on the outcome of the election. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez accused the right-wing Popular Party of planning to undermine inflation-linked increases, while opposition leaders maintained they would continue annual adjustments if elected.
response: Authorities reported 25,000 demonstrators attended the march. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez pledged to protect pensions and accused the opposition Popular Party of planning to weaken inflation-linked increases.

updates.text: Organisers reported 50,000 participants at the Madrid demonstration, while government authorities counted 25,000.
